title: Attached pronouns
blurb: Short pronouns that join the end of a word: my, your, his, her, and him, it, them.
hero_html:
STAGE 3 · UNIT 2

Pronouns that hold on

Some pronouns are written joined to the end of another word: كِتَابُهُ his book, عَلَيْهِ on it, فَتَحَهُ he opened it.

المُتَّصِلَةُ

page_html:
STAGE 3 · UNIT 2

Pronouns that hold on

Some pronouns are written joined to the end of another word: كِتَابُهُ his book, عَلَيْهِ on it, فَتَحَهُ he opened it.

المُتَّصِلَةُ

1The twelve attached pronouns

An attached pronoun cannot stand alone. It joins the end of a noun, a preposition or a verb. Like the separate pronouns, it is fixed.

PronounWhoOn a nounEnglish
ـيI, meكِتَابِيmy book
ـنَاwe, usكِتَابُنَاour book
ـكَyou (one man)كِتَابُكَyour book
ـكِyou (one woman)كِتَابُكِyour book
ـكُمَاyou (two)كِتَابُكُمَاyour book
ـكُمْyou (men, or mixed)كِتَابُكُمْyour book
ـكُنَّyou (women)كِتَابُكُنَّyour book
ـهُhe, itكِتَابُهُhis book
ـهَاshe, itكِتَابُهَاher book
ـهُمَاthey (two)كِتَابُهُمَاtheir book
ـهُمْthey (men, or mixed)كِتَابُهُمْtheir book
ـهُنَّthey (women)كِتَابُهُنَّtheir book
Tip: Compare with unit 1: أَنْتُمَا and ـكُمَا, أَنْتُمْ and ـكُمْ, أَنْتُنَّ and ـكُنَّ. The ـكَ family is "you". The ـهُ family is "he, she, they".

2On a noun: the owner

A pronoun on a noun shows who owns it. It works like the second word of an iḍāfa.

كِتَابُ زَيْدٍ ← كِتَابُهُ
Zayd's book → his book
زَيْدٍ is the owner, jarr. ـهُ takes its job.
كِتَابُهُ جَدِيدٌ.
His book is new.
ـهُ is the owner. It is fixed, so it is in the place of jarr: فِي مَحَلِّ جَرٍّ.
بَيْتُهَا قَرِيبٌ.
Her house is near.
ـهَا is the owner, in the place of jarr.
No ال, no tanween. A noun with an attached pronoun is the first word of an iḍāfa. So it has no ال and no tanween: كِتَابٌ becomes كِتَابُهُ.

The noun still shows its own ending before the pronoun. Only the noun is flexible. The pronoun stays the same.

كِتَابُهُ جَدِيدٌ.
His book is new.
كِتَابُ is the Topic: rafʿ, damma.
قَرَأَ الطَّالِبُ كِتَابَهُ.
The student read his book.
كِتَابَ is the object: naṣb, fatha.
القَلَمُ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
The pen is in his book.
كِتَابِ is after فِي: jarr, kasra.
Tip: A word ending in ة writes it as ت before a pronoun: سَيَّارَةٌ → سَيَّارَتُهُ, غُرْفَةٌ → غُرْفَتُهَا.

3With ـي the ending is hidden

The pronoun ـي always needs a kasra before it. So the noun cannot show damma, fatha or kasra of its own.

كِتَابِي جَدِيدٌ.
My book is new.
كِتَابِ is the Topic and rafʿ, but you see a kasra.
القَلَمُ فِي كِتَابِي.
The pen is in my book.
Here كِتَابِ is jarr. It looks the same.
Do not read the ending before ـي. Before ـي the kasra is for the pronoun. Find the job of the noun from the sentence, never from this vowel.

4On a preposition

A pronoun after a preposition is jarr, like any word after a preposition. It is fixed, so it is in the place of jarr.

القَلَمُ لَكَ.
The pen is yours (for you).
ـكَ is after لِ, in the place of jarr.
خَرَجَ مِنْهُ.
He went out of it.
ـهُ is after مِنْ, in the place of jarr.
الكِتَابُ عَلَيْهِ.
The book is on it.
ـهِ is after عَلَى, in the place of jarr.

Some prepositions change their shape. Learn these forms:

Preposition+ ـهُ+ ـكَ+ ـي
فِيفِيهِفِيكَفِيَّ
عَلَىعَلَيْهِعَلَيْكَعَلَيَّ
إِلَىإِلَيْهِإِلَيْكَإِلَيَّ
مِنْمِنْهُمِنْكَمِنِّي
لِلَهُلَكَلِي
Three changes to remember. عَلَى becomes عَلَيْـ and إِلَى becomes إِلَيْـ: عَلَيْهِ، إِلَيْهَا. لِ becomes لَ: لَهُ، لَكَ، لَهَا. Only with ـي it stays لِي.

5When ـهُ becomes ـهِ

After kasra or ي. After a kasra or a ي, the damma of ـهُ becomes a kasra: فِيهِ، عَلَيْهِ، إِلَيْهِ، بِهِ (with it), فِي بَيْتِهِ.

The same happens to ـهُمَا، ـهُمْ، ـهُنَّ:

عَلَيْهِمْ
on them
ـهُمْ after ي becomes ـهِمْ.
فِيهِمَا
in them (two)
ـهُمَا after ي becomes ـهِمَا.
فِي بَيْتِهِنَّ
in their house (women)
بَيْتِ ends in kasra, so ـهُنَّ becomes ـهِنَّ.
Tip: It is the same pronoun. Only the sound changes, to make it easy to say. With a damma, fatha or sukūn before it, it stays ـهُ: مِنْهُ، لَهُ، كِتَابُهُ.

6On a verb: the object

A pronoun from this table on a past verb or an order verb is the object. The object is naṣb. The pronoun is fixed, so it is in the place of naṣb: فِي مَحَلِّ نَصْبٍ.

فَتَحَ البَابَ ← فَتَحَهُ
He opened the door → he opened it
ـهُ takes the place of البَابَ.
فَتَحَتْهُ البِنْتُ.
The girl opened it.
The pronoun comes right after the verb, before the doer.
كَتَبَهَا المُدَرِّسُ.
The teacher wrote it (the letter).
ـهَا is the object, in the place of naṣb.
اِقْرَأِ الكِتَابَ ← اِقْرَأْهُ
Read the book → read it
The order verb keeps its sukūn: اِقْرَأْ + ـهُ.
اُكْتُبْهُ
Write it.
ـهُ is the object, in the place of naṣb.
Tip: Past verbs also have endings like ـتُ، ـتَ، ـنَا for the doer: "I", "you", "we". They are pronouns too. We learn them in unit 6.
Tip: On a verb, "me" is ـنِي, with an extra ن. We meet it later.

In short

  1. Twelve attached pronouns: ـي، ـنَا، ـكَ، ـكِ، ـكُمَا، ـكُمْ، ـكُنَّ، ـهُ، ـهَا، ـهُمَا، ـهُمْ، ـهُنَّ.
  2. On a noun it is the owner, in the place of jarr. The noun loses ال and tanween.
  3. After a preposition it is in the place of jarr: عَلَيْهِ، إِلَيْكَ، لَهُ.
  4. On a verb it is the object, in the place of naṣb: فَتَحَهُ.
  5. ـهُ becomes ـهِ after kasra or ي. Before ـي the noun's ending is hidden.
